recipes.name: Southwest White Chicken Chili
ingredients_raw: 4 (4 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cut into cubes
2 (15 ounce) cans white kidney beans (cannellini), rinsed and drained
1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Chicken Soup (Regular or 98% Fat Free)

steps.text: Heat oil in a 4-quart saucepan over medium-high heat. Add chicken, onion, bell pepper, chili powder, and cumin; cook until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender, stirring often.
Stir in beans, corn, condensed soup, and water and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Sprinkle with Cheddar and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Southwest White Chicken Chili
raw_recipe.description: This Southwestern-style chicken chili is easy to make with cubed chicken, spices, canned cannellini beans, frozen corn, and shredded Cheddar cheese.

review.reviewBody: This chili was DELICIOUS and so easy to make! It has a nice little kick to it that makes it really stand out. I LOVE LOVE LOVED this recipe!

I enjoyed this recipe immensely, and as I am terrible following any kind of recipe I made some key changes that made it a 10 for us! For starters, I actually cooked the chicken, green pepper, and onion in the same pot that I made the chili in with all the spices to which I included fresh minced garlic, salt, and pepper. I followed everything else except that I added 2 cans of diced tomatoes and used chicken broth instead of water - 1 Can. Then, we added sour cream and cheese to our individual bowls to taste, and it was superb! We had some friends over and we finished off the entire thing like it was going out of style. With cornbread, this is definitely one we'll be eating again and again. Thank you for sharing!

I sprayed my pan with Pam instead of using veg oil. I cooked the onion and pepper with the seasonings until tender. I added the remaining ingredients including a packet of taco seasoning and kidney beans instead of the white beans. I used the meat from a precooked rotisserie chicken to save time. I also added a can of Rotel tomatoes. It turned out great. Will definitely make this again with the above changes.

I found that this tasted better the second day after I added some salt and pepper. Also it needed to cook a bit longer so the onions and peppers could soften more. Great flavor and very easy. Added to my favorites!

I make this recipe and love it. Sometimes I make it without cream of chicken because I sometimes have an asthmatic reaction to those creams but with or without it is very delicious. I actually only make this in the crockpot and I add garlic and red bell pepper to the recipe. I add the cheese when it is done cooking. I've also served it with different things at request : hot sauce, cornbread, Doritos, tortillas, salsa, taco sauce, collard greens or garlic bread.

This is a really good recipe for when you want to make a quick meal. I substituted the water with chicken broth, and ended up adding another cup to add more “juice”. I also added a cup of shredded Monterey Jack cheese to thicken it up a little. We topped ours with tortilla strips, sour cream, and jalapeños. Perfect for a winter day!

Not my favorite ~
Tasted before adding the Campbell's soup and it was awful. So I took other's suggestions & added pepper flakes, a bit of salt & garlic. Better but not good - I added the cream of chicken soup ad it was much improved but still just not 'it'. I then added 2-3 oz salsa and thought it was now 'ok'. May be the corn takes it from 'ok' to 'wonderful' ~ I'll find out tomorrow when I serve it :0

This was very good. I cooked it in the slow cooker. I put my chicken breast in there with everything else and let it cook, then shredded the chicken. I made my own cream of chicken soup. I found it a little thick so thinned it out with chicken broth. I subbed green chillies for the peppers. Topped with sour cream and cheese.

Wonderful recipe! Not Texas Chile but a great alternative. I did play with the recipe a bit. Used 2 cans of chopped green chili’s in place of bell pepper and increased the chili powder and cumin because it was too bland for us. Also used chicken stock in place of water and used more than called for because it needed more liquid. That was my personal taste. Hubby

This is such a wonderful quick, easy recipe. It tastes like it spent all day simmering but really only takes 30 minutes. I had a few modifications that made this so AWESOME my daughter liked it better than Cheesecake Factory's.

1- I added about 50% more chili powder and cumin as others mentioned it was a little bland

2- I used two small cans (2oz ea maybe) of mild chilis instead of fresh green pepper (it gave a better Southwest taste and the peppers pretty much disintegrated into the broth)

3- Instead of water, I used beer. For this, I would suggest an American Lager; I used Miller Lite. I then added water to thin the broth a little as I didn't want it so thick.

4- I did not add corn but when serving added tortilla strips and grated cheese on top.

I think it tastes best with some hot pepper sauce added to it (Louisiana or such) but this addition is probably best once served as others might not be inclined.

Love this recipe! I don't always have the exact ingredients on hand. For example I use sweet peppers when I don't have green (very colorful) and chopped rotisserie chicken makes a quick & delicious change. A MUST at our house is the addition of one chopped jalapeño pepper and two minced garlic cloves. This chili is a definite hit!
This is really tasty. Filling, easy to make, and easy to adapt to your own taste.

I changed the recipe a little, i did not use the 1 (10.5 ounce) can Campbell's condensed cream of chicken soup. I wanted to reduce the calories and use cleaner ingredients. I used 1 1/2 cans of petite diced tomatoes instead . The favorites are great.
Delicious I put a little cayenne in my one to make it a little spicy

Loved this! I added a bit of extra chicken and a packet of taco seasonings (per another recommendation) - served it with Pillsbury cornbread muffins, and sour cream, cheese, and avocados on top - so delish!
This chili was fantastic! Just finished feeding the family and it was a hit. Will make it again.
This was amazing!! I added a can of tomatoes, seasoned salt and garlic .
I added freshly chopped cilantro and a can of jalapenos - this was fantastic.
Love it! Used a seasoning packet instead because the only spices in the cabinet are salt and pepper and about a 1/4 of a medium onion.
I made it, but it wasn’t that great. Directions were easy to follow thou.
